newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK DEPO PLAN SEEN AFFECTING 30 PCT OF IMPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK DEPO PLAN SEEN AFFECTING 30 PCT OF IMPORTS.

text.p: A Slovak government measure imposing a 20 percent deposit on imports will affect volumes equal to around one third of last year's overall imports, the Economics Ministry said on Wednesday.

"After the first analysis based on last year's volumes and import structure we expect the import deposits to affect around 30 percent of the overall volume of 1996 imports," Economics Ministry spokesman Jozef Sucha told Reuters.
Slovakia's imports totalled 335.165 billion last year.

Last week the government ordered all importers of selected consumer and agricultural goods to deposit a sum equal to 20 percent of the value of the imports in non-interest bearing accounts in banks for 180 days.
Sucha said the ministry expected the measure to become effective on May 5.

Local banks have been awaiting decision on how the funds collected from import deposits will be used, saying that the money could increase liquidity in the banking sector if they are held in commercial banks.
But National Bank of Slovakia Governor Vladimir Masar said last week the money should stay in the central bank to drain funds from the market.
Masar added that the NBS might ease its policy by lowering minimum reserves requirements for commercial banks if the funds collected from import deposits were held in the central bank.
Masar had been due to present the NBS position on import deposits at Wednesday's government session.

But government spokeswoman Magda Pospisilova told Reuters after a weekly government meeting it was not yet clear whether the cabinet would discuss the item today or whether it would postpone it until next Tuesday's session.
